payload.name: ExtractExplicitActionsFromIncidentResponses
payload.description: When a user describes a past incident and explicitly lists actions they took in response, extract and preserve each specific action as event details instead of generalizing into a relationship or trait.
content: During extraction, if a message contains a direct answer to a question about what someone did (e.g., how they handled an incident), extract every explicitly named action as a separate event detail in the candidate. Do not replace the actions with a general statement about the relationship, bond, or trait.

When updating an existing memory with a message that lists specific actions, preserve the already-known event facts and add the new concrete actions; avoid changing an event memory into a relationship memory unless the message itself supports that broader category.
Prefer memory kinds that capture the action (event) over abstract kinds (relationship/profile) when the message primarily reports what the person did.

solves: Construction agents often collapse explicit behavioral details (e.g., petting, hugging, speaking calmly, slow walking) into abstract relationship statements, leaving required facts missing. This Skill applies to any future message where a speaker enumerates concrete actions in response to a question or incident; it instructs extraction to capture and retain each explicit action, while not requiring knowledge of the gold answer.
